entities.summary:
Albert I of Käfernburg was a prominent religious figure in medieval Germany, playing a pivotal role in shaping religious practice and spiritual communities from 1170 to 1232. His influence can be seen in the widespread adoption of his theological ideas, which were later codified in the \
\\"Käfernburgian Canon\\\\", a foundational text of the medieval Church.\\\n\\nThrough his leadership, Käfernburg helped to establish a network of monasteries and churches across Western Europe, fostering a sense of unity and cooperation among religious institutions.\\\n\\nHis legacy extended beyond the medieval period, with his ideas influencing the development of Christianity during the Renaissance and the Reformation.\\\n\\nA lasting testament to his impact is the continued veneration of Käfernburg as a patron saint of spiritual seekers and those struggling with religious doubt.
